body.statement: Open-ended Question 6. Using the second-order pair-orbit selection handle, characterize \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\) exactly for every analyst-specified sensitivity sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\): give necessary and sufficient contact conditions inside \(\mathcal F_\rho\), prove recovery by exact finite minimizers rather than merely first-order-optimal designs, and determine how the answer changes with the local approach of \(s_J-J/2\) at \(\rho=1/2\).
body.justification: Exact finite optimizers may select a strict subset of the flat first-order face, and that selection is the proposal's genuinely unresolved theorem-level content.
body.gap: The Airy expansion of SudijonoDobribanTchetgen2026 selects a scalar unrestricted rule, but no published result handles a measure-valued design face, pair-type boundary experiments, or critical hard-budget sequences.
body.consumer: The answer determines which first-order-equivalent laws are exact finite minimax choices at each high-mismatch sensitivity path and supplies a principled tie-breaker for design sensitivity analysis.

obligation.what_is_open: A necessary-and-sufficient contact characterization of \(\mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\) inside \(\mathcal F_\rho\) that recovers limits by exact finite minimizers for every sequence with \(s_J/J\to\rho\ge1/2\).
obligation.obstruction: The first-order lower game is flat on \(\mathcal F_\rho\), while the frozen limiting-experiment handle specifies no local scaling, limiting kernel, second-order risk, or uniform epiconvergence theorem. The exact finite conic certificates determine every fixed \(J\) but do not by themselves identify which contact points persist under \(J\to\infty\), especially when \(s_J-J/2\) changes on a smaller scale.
obligation.attempted: The scalar and two-parameter shrinking-prior experiments were solved, including singular boundary information, and matched by a balanced-orbit centered estimator. They yield the sharp value and the exact first-order envelope. Expanding the resulting information game cannot distinguish two measures with the same balance and mean-mixed constraints; replacing exact minimizers by \(o(J^{-1})\)-optimal procedures therefore loses precisely the selection information requested by the OEQ.
obligation.partial_result:
The exact finite contact system of Theorem 1 makes every set \(\mathcal Q^*(J,s_J)\) computable, and Theorem 5 proves
\[
 \mathcal Q^*_{\infty}[(s_J)]\subseteq\mathcal F_\rho.
\]
It also recovers every \(\mu\in\mathcal F_\rho\) by procedures whose excess worst risk is \(o(J^{-1})\). The unresolved distinction is precisely replacement of those first-order procedures by exact finite minimizers.
